text: Morning. Can we start with the parser bug from yesterday? The timestamp regex is still failing on some transcripts.
Sure. The regex breaks when a speaker label has a colon inside the brackets. The greedy match eats the whole line.
Right, the greedy match grabs everything up to the last colon, so the speaker label swallows the text.
I reproduced it with a fixture that has nested brackets and a timestamp in the middle of the line.
Does the fixture cover the hour format too, or only minutes and seconds in the timestamp?
Only minutes and seconds. The parser treats a three digit hour as a speaker label, which is another edge case.
So two bugs. The greedy match on the colon, and the hour edge case in the timestamp regex.
Yes. A lazy match fixes the colon problem. The hour edge case needs a separate unit test.
I'll write the unit test for the hour edge case this afternoon.
Good. I'll fix the greedy match in the regex and add the nested brackets fixture to the parser suite.
Should we also run the parser over the old transcripts to see how many lines it drops?
Maybe. A dry run over the archive would show whether the regex change shifts any speaker label.
The parser also logs a warning per dropped line, so the dry run output would tell us the edge case count.
Agreed. The warning count from the parser is a decent signal for the regex change.
What about the unicode colon? Some transcripts use a full width colon after the speaker label.
That one is rare. We could normalize the colon before the regex runs, as a later parser fix.
Fine, keep the unicode colon out of this patch. The greedy match and the hour timestamp come first.
Understood. The parser patch will have the lazy match, the fixture, and the unit test for the hour edge case.
And the fixture should keep one line with nested brackets and a colon inside the speaker label.
Yes, the nested brackets fixture already has that line. The regex test asserts the speaker label exactly.
The lazy match also changes how the parser handles a trailing colon with no text after the speaker label.
An empty line after the speaker label should parse as an empty turn, not drop the timestamp.
Then the fixture needs an empty turn case too, next to the nested brackets case.
Yes, add the empty turn to the fixture. The unit test can assert the timestamp survives.
Okay. The regex test grows by three cases: nested brackets, empty turn, and the hour timestamp.
How long until the parser patch is ready for review, roughly?
A day for the regex and the fixture. The unit test review can happen in parallel.
Great, that covers the parser bug for now.
Next item is the release notes for the version going out at the end of the month.
The changelog has every merged change, but the release notes need highlights a reader can scan.
Agreed. Three or four highlights at the top of the release notes, then the full changelog below.
One highlight is the breaking change in the config file. That needs a migration guide link.
The migration guide is half written. The breaking change section should show the old and new config keys.
Let's put a before and after config snippet in the release notes right under the breaking change.
I'll draft the release notes highlights tomorrow and share the draft in the channel.
Should we tag the version before the release notes are final, or wait for the draft review?
We should wait. The version tag goes on the commit that also updates the changelog and the release notes.
Makes sense. The changelog entry and the version tag in one commit keeps the release clean.
Do we want screenshots in the release notes? The settings panel changed a lot in this version.
Maybe two screenshots of the settings panel. More than that and the release notes get heavy.
Two screenshots then. I'll capture them on a clean profile so the settings panel looks default.
The changelog also lists the deprecated flags. Those belong next to the breaking change in the highlights.
Right, deprecated flags and the breaking change together, with the migration guide link after them.
How about a short upgrade checklist at the end of the release notes for people skipping a version?
A skip version upgrade checklist would help. It can reuse the migration guide steps.
Good. So the release notes draft has highlights, the breaking change, deprecated flags, screenshots and the upgrade checklist.
Who reads the release notes first? Mostly admins checking the breaking change before they upgrade.
Then the breaking change goes first in the highlights, before the new features.
And the new features get one line each in the release notes, with the changelog holding the details.
The changelog format also needs a cleanup. Some entries have no version heading at all.
We could add a changelog lint check that fails when an entry lacks a version heading.
A changelog lint check is cheap. It runs in the release workflow before the tag step.
Okay, the release workflow runs the changelog lint, then the version tag, then publishes the release notes.
That is the whole draft. The version tag waits until the draft review is done.
Onboarding docs next. Two new hires start soon and the setup guide is out of date.
The setup guide still shows the old install steps. Half the commands moved to the bootstrap script.
So the install steps section should just say run the bootstrap script and check the output.
Yes, and the onboarding docs need a troubleshooting section for the permissions prompt on first launch.
The permissions prompt confuses everyone. A screenshot of the microphone permission dialog would help the new hires.
I'll add the permission dialog screenshot to the troubleshooting section of the onboarding docs.
What about a walkthrough video for the setup guide? Ten minutes, screen only, no voice over.
A walkthrough video goes stale fast. Maybe a short one that only covers the bootstrap script and the permissions prompt.
Fair. A short walkthrough video for the bootstrap script, and the setup guide holds the details.
The onboarding checklist also needs an owner. Right now new hires ask in the channel who grants repository access.
Let's put the repository access request at the top of the onboarding checklist with the form link.
Good idea. The checklist order would be repository access, bootstrap script, permissions prompt, then the first build.
And the first build step should mention the long model download, otherwise new hires think it froze.
Right. The model download takes a while on the first build. The setup guide can show the expected size.
I will rewrite the install steps in the setup guide this week.
Then I'll review the onboarding docs once your setup guide rewrite lands.
Could we also ask the new hires to note every confusing step in the onboarding checklist during their first week?
Yes, a feedback column in the onboarding checklist. The new hires fill it in as they go.
That gives us a list of fixes for the setup guide after each new hires cohort.
And the troubleshooting section grows from that feedback instead of from guesses.
One more thing for the onboarding docs: the glossary page has dead links to the old wiki.
We could fix the glossary dead links in the same pass as the setup guide rewrite.
The onboarding docs also link a setup guide for the old laptop image that nobody uses now.
Delete that old laptop image page from the onboarding docs and redirect the link to the setup guide.
Fine. The redirect keeps old bookmarks working for anyone who saved the onboarding link.
The new hires also need the editor settings. The setup guide can point to the shared settings file.
Good, a shared editor settings file in the setup guide saves the new hires an hour of tweaking.
Okay, the glossary goes with the setup guide rewrite.
Quick return to the parser bug. While we talked I ran the dry run over the archive with the regex change.
Oh nice. How many lines did the parser drop with the lazy match?
The parser dropped nine lines in the whole archive, all with the three digit hour timestamp edge case.
So the greedy match fix works, and only the hour edge case remains in the timestamp regex.
Exactly. The warning count matched the dropped lines, so the parser logging is accurate.
Then the hour unit test I write today should use one of those nine lines as the fixture.
I'll paste the nine lines into the fixture file so the unit test uses real timestamp shapes.
Great. Can the regex accept one to three hour digits without matching a speaker label by mistake?
Yes, anchor the timestamp regex on the opening bracket and limit the hour to three digits.
The nested brackets fixture should still pass with that anchor. Run the parser suite before pushing.
Will do. I'll run the full parser suite with the new anchor and the nested brackets fixture before the push.
And note the dry run numbers in the pull request so the regex change has evidence.
Sure, the pull request gets the dry run counts and the dropped line samples.
Did the dry run touch the unicode colon lines at all?
Two lines had the unicode colon. The parser kept them, but the speaker label came out wrong.
Then the unicode colon normalize step really is a separate parser fix later. Not in this patch.
Agreed, separate patch. I will file it so the unicode colon case is tracked.
Good, the parser is settled.
Last big item, the cloud bill. The monthly spend went up again and the budget review is next week.
Most of the monthly spend is the storage bucket for the raw recordings. Retention is set to forever.
Forever retention on the storage bucket explains it. What would a ninety day retention policy save?
Roughly forty percent of the storage cost. The raw recordings older than ninety days are rarely read.
Then the retention policy is the first lever. The compute instances are the second.
The compute instances run all night for the batch jobs. Reserved capacity would cut that cost by a third.
Reserved capacity needs a one year commitment. Is the batch load stable enough for that budget?
The batch load has been flat for six months. Reserved capacity for the baseline compute instances looks safe.
What about egress? The cloud bill shows a spike in egress from the storage bucket last month.
The egress spike came from a misconfigured sync job pulling the whole storage bucket every night.
So fixing the sync job removes the egress spike, and the retention policy shrinks the storage bucket.
Yes. With both, the monthly spend drops back under the budget line.
We should set cost alerts so the next egress spike shows up in days, not on the monthly cloud bill.
Cost alerts at eighty and one hundred percent of the monthly budget would catch it.
Let's set the cost alerts today, before anything else changes.
I'll set up the cost alerts on the budget this afternoon and send the thresholds to the channel.
I'll fix the sync job schedule so it only pulls new recordings, which ends the egress spike.
And the retention policy change on the storage bucket needs sign off before we apply it.
I will write a one page cost summary for the budget review with the retention policy and reserved capacity numbers.
How about including the egress spike chart in the cost summary? It makes the sync job story obvious.
Yes, the egress chart goes in the cost summary next to the monthly spend trend.
Should we price reserved capacity for two years too, just to compare against the one year commitment?
Maybe, if the cloud pricing page makes it quick. The one year reserved capacity is the main option.
Got it. The cost summary covers retention policy, reserved capacity, the egress spike and cost alerts.
Sounds good, I'll book the budget review slot for the cost summary next week.
The cloud bill also has a line for idle compute instances in the test account.
Idle compute instances in the test account should shut down at night. That is free money.
A nightly shutdown schedule for the test account compute instances is easy to add.
What does the idle compute cost per month, ballpark, on the cloud bill?
About a tenth of the monthly spend. Smaller than the storage bucket, but it adds up over the budget year.
Put the idle compute instances in the cost summary too, as the quick win.
Okay, the quick win is the nightly shutdown, the big lever is the retention policy on the storage bucket.
And the reserved capacity is the slow lever, since the commitment needs budget approval.
Right, the reserved capacity purchase goes through the budget review, not before.
We might also tag every storage bucket with an owner so the cloud bill splits cost by team.
Owner tags on each storage bucket would make the cost alerts point at the right team.
Then the budget review has everything: the storage bucket retention, compute instances and the cloud bill trend.
Okay, recap. Parser fix and the hour unit test, the release notes draft, the setup guide rewrite, and the cost alerts.
That matches my list. I'll send the recap notes in the channel after the call.
Thanks, talk tomorrow.
